get.description:
The plugin calls this on a schedule with the slugs it knows about and gets
back one small object per listing. This is what turns "it sold on AGT" into
"the WooCommerce product is out of stock" without AGT ever having to reach
into the dealer's store, which is exactly what most dealer sites (behind a
WAF, on a private host) could not accept anyway.

delete.summary:
Soft-delete. Reversible: the images survive, so restore() brings the
listing back whole. Trashing a product in WooCommerce lands here

post.summary:
Un-delete. Restoring a product from the WooCommerce trash lands here, which
is what makes the two sides symmetrical

StoreDealerListingRequest.description:
Create a listing through the dealer API.

The rules mirror CreatePostRequest (the web wizard) via the shared
ListingRules, so a WooCommerce product cannot get onto AGT under looser terms
than one typed in by hand. The differences are only in shape: this endpoint
takes JSON-ish field names and real file uploads, not the wizard's
existing_images/reorder machinery.
StoreDealerListingRequest.title: StoreDealerListingRequest

UpdateDealerListingRequest.description:
Partially update a listing through the dealer API.

Every field is optional: a WooCommerce store that only changed a price sends
only the price. When a field IS present it faces exactly the same rules as on
create (via the shared ListingRules), so an update can never sneak past a
constraint that create enforces.
